central_question: Does continuous production of heritably stable colonial offspring without manual serial selection demonstrate independent daughter establishment after all reproductive intervention and habitat rescue ends?

sources.grade_of_this_review: E2 main text from author-uploaded original; original figures/raw records not checked
sources.rights: Publisher reuse terms not established; ResearchGate author upload flagged copyright; paraphrase only
sources.experiment_unit: chemostat culture; replication reported about 70% but exact number not provided
sources.positive: predator selection yielded stable ~eight-celled photosynthetic colonies; budding parent colonies released new daughter colonies; colonies maintained in light in continuous or monospecific culture
sources.negative: small colonies predation-prone; darkness causes stage-two washout; entire ecology requires pump, nutrient reservoir, light and habitat
supports: continuous chemostat population without manually selected transfer every generation
does_not_support: independent daughter colonization of unprepared sites

sources.grade_of_this_review: E2 full main Methods Results Discussion
sources.historical_catalog_evidence_grade: E1; unchanged pending separate catalog reconciliation
sources.rights: CC BY 4.0 main article; third-party/supplementary rights not independently checked
sources.experiment_unit: five predator-exposed lines vs three controls, shared F1 starting cross; multiple isolates nested in two successful lines
sources.positive: 2/5 evolved multicellular characteristics, stable for four years in maintained predator-free culture; clonally derived multicellular propagules observed for some isolates, predator-defense assay beneficial
sources.negative: 3/5 predator lines did not establish stable multicellular histories; some isolates from successful lines remained unicellular; some colonies gathered unattached swim cells
supports: physical parent-to-daughter propagules in defined culture
does_not_support: independent replication of overlapping 2025 Chen group

sources.grade_of_this_review: E2 free-access original Methods Results Discussion
sources.rights: Free publisher access, CC license not established; Dryad data not reanalysed
sources.experiment_unit: 15 separately destructively sampled microcosms per treatment over five days; no independent evolved origins
sources.positive: live predators and filtered supernatant induce algal grouping, more intense with predator density
sources.negative: predator-exposed and control groups not distinguishable by individually tested day-20 contrasts, after predators decreased; direct demonstration of inherited life cycle absent
sources.caveat: Rapid evolutionary sorting after predator loss not excluded by authors; overall day-20 F test significant despite individual contrasts non-significant; fresh medium transferred on day 10
does_not_support: failed replication of Boraas under same protocol

prior_canonical_comparator.negative: 0/12 settling-selected groups had stable heritable multicellularity compared with 4/12 predator-selected; two inferred founders, overlapping Herron methods/network

study_independence: Boraas, Herron and Fisher use distinct experimental programs, predator taxa, habitat scales and times; not directly pooled independent replications of one closure proposition; Chen 2025 shares some researcher lineage with Herron 2019.

falsifiable_future_only_hypotheses.topic: continuous budding in chemostat versus daughter settlement without re-seeding
heritable phenotype stability versus independently established descendants
predator-cue induction and evolution can be confused
